The '''Premier League Manager of the Season''' is an annual [[association football]] award presented to [[Manager (association football)|managers]] in England. It recognises the most outstanding manager in the [[Premier League]] each season. The recipient is chosen by a panel assembled by the league's [[Premier League#Sponsorship|sponsors]] and is announced in the second or third week of May.<ref name="Eight">{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/7401795.stm|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|date=14 May 2008 |access-date=16 December 2011|title= Ronaldo & Ferguson win top awards}}</ref> The award was established during the [[1993–94 FA Premier League|1993–94 season]] by then-league title sponsor [[Carling brewery|Carling]]. For sponsorship purposes, it was called the Carling Manager of the Year from 1994 to 2001, the [[Barclaycard]] Manager of the Year from 2001 to 2004, and since 2004 known as the '''[[Barclays]] Manager of the Season'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://blogs.independent.co.uk/2011/05/23/too-many-awards-in-football-make-them-worthless/ |work=[[The Independent]] |date=23 May 2011 |access-date=16 December 2011 |last=Rice |first=Simon |title=Too many awards in football make them worthless |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131011003028/http://blogs.independent.co.uk/2011/05/23/too-many-awards-in-football-make-them-worthless/ |archive-date=11 October 2013 }}</ref>

In 1994, the inaugural Manager of the Season award was given to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] manager [[Alex Ferguson|Sir Alex Ferguson]] for retaining the league championship.<ref name="League">{{Cite web |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/spl/aberdeen/ferguson-s-secret-has-led-to-a-united-stand-1.706434|work=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]|date=14 May 1994 |access-date=16 December 2011|last=Traynor|first=James|title=Ferguson's secret has led to a United stand }}</ref> The current holder of the award is [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] manager [[Mikel Arteta]].

The most awards won by a single manager is eleven, achieved by Sir Alex Ferguson between 1994 and his retirement in 2013. He accounted for more than half of the awards in that period of time. In 1998 [[Arsène Wenger]] became the first non-British manager to win the award, and received it on two further occasions with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]. [[José Mourinho]], [[Pep Guardiola]] and Jürgen Klopp are the only managers other than Sir Alex Ferguson and Wenger to have won the award on more than on one occasion, with the two first being the only managers other than Ferguson to win the award in consecutive seasons.

Five managers have won the award without winning the Premier League trophy in the same season, reflecting the weight of their achievements: [[George Burley]] in 2000–01, having guided [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] to fifth place in the league, after only securing the club's promotion from the First Division the previous season;<ref name="Burley">{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/1342681.stm|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=21 May 2001 |access-date=16 December 2011| title= Burley scoops top manager award}}</ref> [[Harry Redknapp]] in 2009–10, for steering [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] to a top-four finish for the first time in twenty years,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sponsorship.barclays.co.uk/barclaysfc/bfc-season/winners/mar10/index.html|publisher=Barclays FC|access-date=16 December 2011|title=Harry Redknapp named Barclays Manager of the Season|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121223094832/http://www.sponsorship.barclays.co.uk/barclaysfc/bfc-season/winners/mar10/index.html|archive-date=23 December 2012}}</ref> [[Alan Pardew]] in 2011–12, having guided [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] to their highest position in nine years,<ref name = Pardew>{{cite web|title=Newcastle United's Alan Pardew named manager of the season|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18042404|work=BBC Sport|access-date=11 May 2012|date=11 May 2012}}</ref> [[Tony Pulis]] in 2013–14, for steering [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] from bottom of the league in November to an 11th-place finish, and [[Jürgen Klopp]] in 2021–22, after finishing second with [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in a tight battle for the title, finishing just one point off the top despite being 14 points behind in January.

==History==
{{see also|Premier League|English football sponsorship|}}
The Premier League was formed in 1992, when the members of the [[Football League First Division|First Division]] resigned from [[The Football League]]. These clubs set up a new commercially independent league that negotiated its own broadcast and sponsorship agreements.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/about/history.html |title=History of the Premier League |publisher=[[Premier League]] |access-date=16 December 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120421110805/http://www.premierleague.com/en-gb/about/history.html |archive-date=21 April 2012 }}</ref> The [[1992–93 FA Premier League|inaugural season]] had no sponsor until Carling agreed to a four-year [[Pound sterling|£]]12&nbsp;million deal that started the [[1993–94 FA Premier League|following season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/1118425.stm|title=Why Carling called time on Premiership|first=Peter|last=Jones|date=19 January 2001|publisher=BBC|work=BBC Sport|access-date=16 November 2011}}</ref> That same season, Carling introduced the [[Premier League Manager of the Month|Manager of the Month]] and Manager of the Season awards,<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061210142537/http://www.premierleague.com/fapl.rac?command=forwardOnly&nextPage=enSeasons |url=http://www.premierleague.com/fapl.rac?command=forwardOnly&nextPage=enSeasons |title=Premier League Awards |publisher=Premier League |archive-date=10 December 2006 |access-date=20 October 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref> in addition to the existing [[League Managers Association Awards#LMA Manager of the Year|manager of the year award]] presented by the [[League Managers Association]].

[[File:2013 Premier League Manager of the Season award.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The award Sir Alex Ferguson received after winning the 2012–13 Premier League season|alt=The 2012–13 PL MotM.]]
The first Manager of the Season award was presented to Sir Alex Ferguson after winning the Premier League with Manchester United for the second consecutive season.<ref name="League"/> Kenny Dalglish was awarded the accolade in the [[1994–95 FA Premier League|1994–95]] season, having guided [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] to their first league title in 81 years.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/kenny-dalglish-at-blackburn-1311105.html|work=[[The Independent]]|date=23 August 1996 |access-date=13 January 2012|title=Kenny Dalglish at Blackburn}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/ewood-park-has-seen-it-all-before--long-long-ago-1619675.html|work=[[The Independent]]|date=15 May 1995 |access-date=13 January 2012|last=Shaw|first=Phil|title=Ewood Park has seen it all before&nbsp;– long, long ago}}</ref> Despite losing to Liverpool on the final matchday, Blackburn secured the championship when Manchester United failed to beat [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] the same day.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/rovers-title-forged-by-hammers-1619690.html|work=[[The Independent]]|date=15 May 1995 |access-date=13 January 2012|last=Moore|first=Glenn|title=Rovers' title forged by Hammers}}</ref> Manchester United regained the Premier League [[1995–96 FA Premier League|the following season]], resisting [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]'s threat, and successfully retained the championship in [[1996–97 FA Premier League|1996–97]], ensuring that Ferguson became the first manager to win two consecutive awards.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/spl/aberdeen/old-trafford-fans-are-ferguson-s-inspiration-1.398652|work=[[The Herald (Glasgow)|The Herald]]|date=13 May 1997|access-date=14 January 2012 |title=Old Trafford fans are Ferguson's inspiration}}</ref>

[[File:Arsene Wenger.JPG|thumb|right|200px|[[Arsène Wenger]], winner in 1998, 2002 and 2004 with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]|alt=In front of building entrance, a white-haired man with a red polo shirt under a dark blue coat looks straight at the camera.]]
Arsène Wenger was the first non–British manager to receive the Manager of the Season award, having led Arsenal to the top of the Premier League in [[1997–98 FA Premier League|1997–98]], his first full season at the club.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/1281890.stm|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=14 May 2001 |access-date=14 January 2012 |title=Top bosses made to wait }}</ref> This achievement was significant given that Arsenal were, at one stage, 12 points behind leaders Manchester United.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/arid-20147343.html|work=[[Irish Examiner]]|date=5 March 2011 |access-date=14 January 2012|last=Stone|first=Simon|title=Angry Fergie comes out fighting}}</ref> After a climactic finish to the [[1998–99 FA Premier League|1998–99]] season, Sir Alex Ferguson was presented with his fifth managerial award for winning the Premier League with Manchester United.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/345385.stm|publisher=BBC |work=BBC News|date=17 May 1999 |access-date=13 January 2012|title=Fergie is top boss }}</ref> The club beat [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] on the last matchday to secure their fifth championship in seven years, and in the following week completed a [[Treble (association football)|treble]] of trophies consisting of the domestic league, [[1999 FA Cup Final|FA Cup]] and [[1999 UEFA Champions League Final|UEFA Champions League]]. Ferguson received the accolade again in [[1999–2000 FA Premier League|1999–2000]], as Manchester United finished 18 points above second-placed Arsenal.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/749585.stm|publisher=BBC |work=BBC News|date=15 May 2000 |access-date=13 January 2012|title=Fergie wins manager award }}</ref>

Ipswich Town manager George Burley was the winner in [[2000–01 FA Premier League|2000–01]], the first time the award did not go to a league-winning manager.<ref name="Burley"/> Ipswich Town, who won promotion to the Premier League from the First Division in the previous season, finished fifth and qualified for the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/1338654.stm|publisher=BBC |work=BBC News|date=19 May 2001 |access-date=14 January 2012|title=Derby dent Ipswich hopes }}</ref> Burley triumphed over Sir Alex Ferguson, who led Manchester United to their third consecutive championship title, and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] manager [[Gérard Houllier]], who guided his team to three trophies and a berth in the Champions League.<ref name="Burley"/> Wenger was named the Manager of the Season for [[2001–02 FA Premier League|2001–02]] after guiding Arsenal to thirteen consecutive wins towards the end of the season&nbsp;– a run which ensured the club regained the Premier League trophy.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/arsenal/1985879.stm|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=13 May 2002 |access-date=13 January 2012|title=Wenger wins double honours }}</ref> For winning his eighth Premier League title with Manchester United, Ferguson was given the award in the [[2002–03 FA Premier League|2002–03]] season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/may/13/newsstory.sport9|work=[[The Guardian]]| date=13 May 2003|access-date=14 January 2012|title=Moyes manager of the year}}</ref> Wenger was the outstanding winner for the award in [[2003–04 FA Premier League|2003–04]] as he managed Arsenal to an unprecedented achievement of winning the league without a single defeat. Reflecting on Wenger's accomplishment, a Barclaycard Awards Panel spokesperson said "Arsène Wenger is a very worthy recipient of this accolade and has sent his team into the history books. Arsenal have played exciting attacking football throughout the season and finishing it unbeaten is a feat that may not be repeated for another 100 years."<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11670_2299422,00.html|work=Sky Sports|access-date=14 January 2012|title=Gunners duo land more awards |first=James|last=Pearson}}</ref>

[[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] manager José Mourinho was chosen as the recipient for the [[2004–05 FA Premier League|2004–05]] season for taking the club to its first league championship in 50 years.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/4544479.stm|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=13 May 2005 |access-date=14 January 2012| title=Chelsea trio scoop season awards}}</ref> Chelsea finished the season with a league-record 95 points,<ref>{{Cite web|title = Wenger: 78–80 points enough for title|url = http://www.espnstar.com/football/premier-league/news/detail/item546550/Wenger:-78-80-points-enough-for-title/|publisher = [[ESPN STAR Sports]]|access-date = 23 January 2012|url-status = usurped|archive-url = https://archive.today/20120730001614/http://www.espnstar.com/football/premier-league/news/detail/item546550/Wenger:-78-80-points-enough-for-title/|archive-date = 30 July 2012}}</ref> 12 points ahead of runners-up Arsenal, scoring 72 goals and conceding 15 in the process.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.statto.com/football/teams/chelsea/2004-2005/table|work=Statto.com|access-date=25 January 2012|title=Chelsea 2004–2005 : English Premier League Table|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131206093752/http://www.statto.com/football/teams/chelsea/2004-2005/table|archive-date=6 December 2013}}</ref> Mourinho won the award a second successive time the [[2005–06 FA Premier League|following season]]&nbsp;– the first foreign manager to do so&nbsp;– as Chelsea won their second Premier League title.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/4752527.stm|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=8 May 2006 |access-date=13 January 2012| title=Mourinho scoops managerial award}}</ref> Sir Alex Ferguson collected the award for the [[2006–07 FA Premier League|2006–07]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sportinglife.com/football/nat1teams/sunderland/news/story_get.cgi?STORY_NAME=soccer/07/05/16/manual_105751.html&TEAMHD=sunderland&DIV=nat1&TEAM=SUNDERLAND&RH=Sunderland&PREV_SEASON=&BID=|work=[[Sporting Life (British newspaper)|sportinglife.com]]|access-date=14 January 2012|title=Keane picks up managerial gong}}{{dead link|date=October 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> [[2007–08 Premier League|2007–08]]<ref name="Eight"/> and [[2008–09 Premier League|2008–09]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/8069391.stm|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=28 May 2009 |access-date=14 January 2012| title=Moyes wins record third LMA award}}</ref> seasons, in a period when Manchester United regained the domestic title after a four-year drought and retained the trophy for a further two years. Tottenham manager Harry Redknapp was presented with the award at the end of the [[2009–10 Premier League|2009–10]] season, having guided the club to fourth position and a spot in the following season's Champions League at the expense of [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/soccer/redknapp-is-named-manager-of-the-season-119258.html|work=[[Irish Examiner]]| date=8 May 2010|access-date=25 August 2020 | title= Redknapp is named manager of the season}}</ref> In May 2011, Sir Alex Ferguson picked up his tenth Manager of the Season award for leading Manchester United to a record 19th league title.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13479964|publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|date=20 May 2011 |access-date=14 January 2012| title=Sir Alex Ferguson and Nemanja Vidic win season awards}}</ref> In May 2012, [[Alan Pardew]] won his first Manager of the Season award after guiding [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] to their highest position in nine years.<ref name="Pardew" /> In May 2013, Sir Alex Ferguson picked up his eleventh Manager of the Season award for leading Manchester United to a record 20th league title.<ref name=ferguson20>{{cite news|language=vi|author=T.Vĩ|title=Alex Ferguson - HLV xuất sắc nhất giải Ngoại hạng Anh năm 2013|url=http://thethao.tuoitre.vn/tin/2013/05/22/cac-mon-khac/alex-ferguson-hlv-xuat-sac-nhat-giai-ngoai-hang-anh-nam-2013/4004.html|access-date=9 March 2014|newspaper=[[Tuổi Trẻ]]|date=22 May 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140309112640/http://thethao.tuoitre.vn/tin/2013/05/22/cac-mon-khac/alex-ferguson-hlv-xuat-sac-nhat-giai-ngoai-hang-anh-nam-2013/4004.html|archive-date=9 March 2014}}</ref> [[Tony Pulis]] became the first Welsh recipient of the award in May 2014, for guiding [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] from bottom place to 11th.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/may/13/luis-suarez-tony-pulis-barclays-awards | work = [[The Guardian]] | access-date = 13 May 2014 | date = 13 May 2014 |title = Luis Suárez and Tony Pulis scoop Barclays Premier League season awards}}</ref>
